data.narrative:
Castelion, a Series B defense and security company founded by Bryon Hargis, Sean Pitt, and Andrew Kreitz, is evaluated against a universe of 10 comparable companies—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers including Dream Security, Harmattan AI, Code Metal, Defense Unicorns, and Heven AeroTech. The target carries a last post-money valuation of $1.0B on $100M raised to date.

Two valuation methods triangulate around the current ask. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-round step-ups, yielding $1.9B. Peer-median analysis across six same-sector, same-stage comparables produces $1.1B; the peer set spans $300M to $3.0B, with Dream Security at the high end ($3.0B) and the lower quartile anchored by Defense Unicorns and Heven AeroTech (both $1.0B). These methods imply a triangulated range of $956M (low), $1.5B (median), and $2.2B (high).

The median implied valuation of $1.5B sits modestly above the current $1.0B valuation. Key uncertainties include wide peer dispersion—particularly Dream Security's $3.0B outlier—and the absence of revenue-based or growth rate metrics to validate relative positioning within the peer cohort. Revenue scale and margin trajectory would sharpen conviction in placement within the $956M–$2.2B band.
